properties.geological_context: Valley and Ridge Province, underlain by folded and faulted Paleozoic sedimentary strata, dominated by Knox Group carbonates, limestone, and dolostone with moderate karst terrain
properties.soil_profile: Dunmore and Dewey silt loams, well-drained, reddish-brown clayey subsoils derived from weathered limestone residuum
properties.topographical_relief: Rolling Appalachian foothill terrain, gently sloping north-northwest toward Watauga watershed

properties.typology: Single-family residential parcel in low-density suburban woodland setting

structures.facade_material: Red Appalachian clay brick veneer combined with horizontal painted weatherboard siding
structures.roof_form: Multi-gabled and hip roofline clad in dark architectural asphalt shingles
structures.fenestration: Double-hung multi-pane sash windows with crisp white casing and raised masonry sill courses

structures.facade_material: Painted timber lap siding, asphalt shingle roofing

properties.civil_infrastructure: Asphalt-paved curvilinear residential driveway leading off Hiwassee Hill Drive, buried electrical/telecom utilities, low concrete perimeter edging

properties.canopy_composition: Mixed Southern Appalachian deciduous-coniferous canopy: Quercus alba (White Oak), Acer rubrum (Red Maple), Liriodendron tulipifera (Tulip Poplar), Pinus virginiana (Virginia Pine), and mature ornamental Japanese Maples with dense understory turf grass (Festuca arundinacea)

properties.atmospheric_haze: Warm amber Appalachian ridge haze, low-angle raking sunlight casting deep elongated shadows across manicured lawn gradients
